reviews.title: Built for corporate 9-to-5s, useless for real 12-hour shift workers
reviews.text:
If you work a complex 12-hour rotation like the 28-day DuPont schedule, save your time and money. Every major shift calendar app fails because they are designed for corporate managers rather than front-line shift workers.
Here is why none of them work:

1. Off-Day Overtime Math Is Broken: Most apps only calculate overtime after you hit 40 weekly hours. In reality, working an off-day is automatically 1.5x overtime pay, regardless of total hours worked that week. There is no simple "Unscheduled Pickup" toggle that applies overtime rates without ruining your underlying schedule.

2. Dynamic 28-Day Rotations Break the App: DuPont schedules swing wildly between 36, 48, and 60 hours depending on the week. Apps force these into rigid weekly templates, making earnings calculations inaccurate.

3. Inflexible Pay Controls: Picking up an extra shift shouldn't require altering your entire repeating pattern. Users need a simple way to manually edit single-day earnings without breaking the baseline rotation.

4. Over-Engineered, Corporate UI: These apps are cluttered with visual bloat, messaging tools, and deep menus. All shift workers need is a clean, simplified visual calendar showing schedule and pay at a glance.

The Fix:
Developers need to separate the baseline schedule from worked days, add an automatic overtime toggle for off-day pickups, and strip away the corporate clutter. Until an app implements these basic features, its pay tracking is useless for 12-hour shift workers.

reviews.title: Not for Oil Field Workers
reviews.text: Deleted the app as soon as it wouldn’t let me put 84 hours as my weekly hours worked. I work 12 hours a day 7 days a week. Thats 84 hours. Why it wouldn’t allow me to input 84 hours, I don’t know. Not interested in spending any more time fiddling with an app that from the beginning is incompatible with me and my work schedule. The UI did feel nice though, hence 2 stars.
